## Introduction

The past simple is the primary tense for **completed actions at a definite past time**. It is the backbone of storytelling in English: events are reported one after another, each finished before the next begins. When a past time is specified (*yesterday, in 2010, two days ago*), the past simple is almost always required.

## Formation

| | Affirmative | Negative | Interrogative |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **All subjects (regular)** | I **worked** | I **did not (didn't) work** | **Did** I **work**? |
| **All subjects (irregular)** | She **went** | She **did not go** | **Did** she **go**? |

Note that after *did/didn't*, the main verb returns to its **base form**: *"Did she **go**?"* (not *"Did she went?"*).

### Spelling Rules for Regular -ed

* Most verbs add **-ed**: *walk → walked*.
* Verbs ending in **-e** add **-d**: *love → loved*.
* **Consonant + y** changes to **-ied**: *study → studied* (but *play → played*).
* One-syllable **vowel + consonant** verbs double the consonant: *stop → stopped*, *plan → planned* (but *visit → visited* — stress on the first syllable).

### Pronunciation of -ed

| Sound | Condition | Examples |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **/t/** | after voiceless sounds (p, k, f, s, ch, sh) | *worked, watched, hoped* |
| **/d/** | after voiced sounds (vowels, b, g, l, m, n, r, v, z) | *played, lived, opened* |
| **/ɪd/** | after **t** or **d** | *wanted, needed, decided* |

## Core Uses

### 1. Completed Actions at a Definite Past Time
* *"I **visited** the museum yesterday."*
* *"They **finished** the project last week."*

### 2. A Sequence of Completed Events (Narrative)
* *"She **opened** the door, **stepped** inside, and **switched** on the light."*

### 3. Past Habits and Repeated Actions
* *"When I was a child, I **played** tennis every Saturday."*
* *"He **called** her three times yesterday."*

### 4. Past States
* *"The ancient Romans **believed** in many gods."*
* *"She **owned** a bookshop for twenty years."*

### 5. Hypothetical Distance and Politeness
The past form can signal unreality or social distance:
* *"If I **had** more time, I'd learn the violin."* (unreal present — second conditional)
* *"I **wondered** whether you could help."* (polite)

## Past Simple vs. Present Perfect

| Past Simple | Present Perfect |
| :--- | :--- |
| Definite finished time | Unspecified time / present relevance |
| *"I **saw** her last night."* | *"I **have seen** her."* |
| *"He **worked** there for ten years."* (no longer) | *"He **has worked** there for ten years."* (still) |
| With *yesterday, ago, in 2010, last week* | With *ever, never, yet, already, since, for* |

## Nuances

* **"Used to" vs. "would":** Both express past habits. *Used to* covers states and habits (*"I **used to** live in Rome"*); *would* is only for repeated actions, never states (*"Every summer we **would** swim in the lake"*).
* **Emphatic *did*:** *"I **did** tell you!"*
* **Negative *used to*:** *"I **didn't use to** like coffee."*

## Common Errors

> ❌ *"Did she went home?"* → ✅ *"Did she **go** home?"*
> ❌ *"I have seen him yesterday."* → ✅ *"I **saw** him yesterday."*
> ❌ *"He stoped the car."* → ✅ *"He **stopped** the car."* (double the consonant)

## Model Sentences

> *"In 1953 he **left** his village, **crossed** the border at night, and **arrived** in the city with nothing but a suitcase — a journey he **never forgot**."*

## Knowledge Check

**1. Choose the correct sentence:**
A) I have finished the report yesterday.
B) I finished the report yesterday.

**2. What is the past simple of "study"?**
A) studyed
B) studied
C) studed

**3. In "If I had a million dollars, I would travel," why is the past simple used?**
A) The action happened in the past.
B) It expresses an unreal present situation.

### Answer Key
1. **B.** A definite past time (*yesterday*) requires the past simple.
2. **B.** Consonant + y → -ied.
3. **B.** The second conditional uses past forms for hypothetical present situations.
